scope: Shared monthly booking calendar and small transparent 3D mode-control illustrations. Task 1 gallery, service presentation, contacts, reviews, navigation and external redirect safeguards are retained.

implementation.calendar: One selected-service calendar with localized month/year, Monday-first seven-column grid, bounded navigation, green available dates, orange selected date, gray diagonal-struck disabled dates and neutral unknown dates.
implementation.sequence: Service -> staff if more than one eligible person -> available date -> actual time -> guest customer details and compact summary -> existing booking POST confirmation.
implementation.availability: Monthly wrapper reuses buildAvailableSlots without changing its algorithm. One public-business read and two business/staff/status/date-scoped busy queries cover a month. A frozen server clock, Europe/Sofia local-day boundaries and UTC storage preserve notice/horizon/DST rules.
implementation.database_safety: Exact busy-row counts must be safe integers equal to returned row counts. Missing, truncated or inconsistent results fail as technical errors rather than creating false availability.
implementation.state_safety: Selection resets on service/staff/month changes. Per-instance four-entry 15-second cache shares identical requests and aborts stale subscriptions. Generation keys reject older responses. Clock updates remove expired server-provided slots only. In-flight booking selections stay immutable until submission unlocks.
implementation.submission: Original payload, guest behavior, consent, notifications and authoritative slot revalidation remain. A synchronous ref lock prevents duplicate POSTs; success requires backend appointment ID/token. SLOT_UNAVAILABLE refreshes availability and clears the time while retaining customer details. Existing PostgreSQL atomic conflict protection is unchanged.
implementation.external_mode: No native calendar is mounted for external-booking businesses. Existing validated/approved outbound URL handling remains; no synthetic dates or additional parameters are introduced.
implementation.artwork: Two locally served lossless WebP illustrations generated with the built-in image tool from the supplied style reference; genuine transparency verified. Each displays at 30 CSS pixels. Full prompts, provenance and hashes are recorded in profile-control-art-20261110.json. No service photos have been invented.

api.response: month, timezone, today, firstBookableDate, lastBookableDate, generatedAt, days[{date,slots[{startsAt,endsAt,localTime,localEndTime,staffId,staffName}]}]
api.security: Strict slug/month/UUID/service/staff validation, external-mode guard, existing public-business eligibility, rate limit 60 requests per minute per existing limiter key, private no-store responses, safe errors and Server-Timing.
api.test_endpoint: POST /api/dev/business-profile/month uses only validated fictional fixture schedules and the real availability engine. Returns 404 before reading input in production. No provider/database dependencies.

verified: Page starts at scrollY=0, gallery remains first, no calendar before service selection, two 30px 3D control assets load.
Service button opens/focuses shared monthly calendar; available date reveals actual fixture-engine slots; time reveals customer form and focuses name.
Month change clears date/time/details panel; staff change clears stale selection; BG/EN month/weekday/status text works.
Injected network failure shows neutral dates and concise Retry; retry restores availability. Empty month has 30 disabled dates, no redundant empty panel, and next-month navigation.
Injected local conflict removes occupied 09:00/09:30 slots and preserves customer-entered values for another slot. No actual booking POST is made by fixture.
External mode contains outbound panel, no native calendar.

limitations: Live guest submission and notification delivery were deliberately not tested. Actual native POST success/conflict behavior is covered offline with injected boundaries. Fake-store race tests cover application error mapping, not proof of PostgreSQL exclusion constraints; existing database tests are part of the full suite.
No buffer field exists in the current schema, so this feature does not introduce a new buffer rule. Existing authoritative engine behavior is preserved.

Availability remains advisory until the existing server submission and atomic conflict guard accept the reservation. Busy data exceeding the database response cap yields a retryable technical error, never invented free dates.
No real service-specific business photos were supplied for this task. Existing rights-cleared illustrations/neutral fallbacks remain until the user supplies photos.
No separate lint script exists in package.json. Production compilation/type validation and the full test suite ran; no unexecuted lint claim is made.
